Inline paths expose complete reviewed differences, authoritative blockers and permitted financial warnings in the card; retained paths expose them in the owning review before approval. The Adaptive Proposal Review Rule derives the path from validated input: metadata patches of up to three fields without a client-reference change and budget submission use an explicit direct action. Client-reference changes, Project Manager assignment, activation, closing, reallocation, budget approval and rejection add one short shared `ConfirmationDialog`. Metadata patches larger than three fields and reallocations affecting more than two categories retain one wide, content-sized `FormSheet`; sensitive decisions retain their confirmation there. Desktop uses `desktopAsideSummary` and `desktopFooterPlacement="aside"`: identity, reviewed rows, human reasons and financial detail belong in the main left pane, with concise grouped summary facts and protected actions in the right aside. Mobile reads the same context and summary in one column, with protected bottom actions. Shared `ReviewCollection` and `ReviewItem` render immutable contextual rows with five-row pagination at every width; static “Rincian” / “Ringkas” reveals supplied supporting facts without selection or inline editing. Preserve page, open row, budget disclosure and overlay ownership through resize and reopening. Reuse `ProposalInlineReview`, labeled `ProposalDiffRow` comparisons with `strikeBefore={false}`, divided wrapping `FactRow` values and `MoneyValue` with `variant="fullDynamic"` for complete, unwrapped rupiah amounts. Reallocation shows each changed category’s before/after allocation, identifies how many categories change and retains the other category allocations; larger reviews keep the full category context in the collection. A plain “Rincian budget” disclosure exposes secondary financial facts within the same review owner. Current action permissions, the applicable budget or profitability grant and the absence of a review error govern financial facts, category amounts and warnings; a failed access or refresh must not leave those values visible. Activation names each authoritative readiness result with an icon and concise status. Server-returned readiness and closing blockers remain the saving barrier and appear through `ProposalReviewFeedback` after project identity and before reviewed values, with recovery attached to its message. Human reallocation and rejection reasons and the closing note use left-aligned, wrapping prose in the main review, inline card and applicable confirmation, rather than compressed summary values. The proposal is immutable: corrections through chat request a fresh proposal from current sources. Streaming, current permissions, readiness, pending, stale and expired states guard explicit confirmation; pending work prevents repeat submission and dismissal, and changed data offers a fresh proposal. Either path sends only the stored proposal identity. The short confirmation repeats project identity, reviewed effect, supplied reason or note and permitted financial consequences before its action. Saved receipts retain the action-specific completed outcome, including the final profitability snapshot for closing, keep the stock/cash status visible and lead to “Buka proyek” on the canonical project route. This family inherits Atria’s Manrope roles, cool canvas, white grouped owners, capsule controls and shared focus, dismissal, sizing and motion without new tokens or another visual world.

rules.name: The AI Bank and Cash Review Rule
rules.body: AI account creation, metadata/theme correction, activation/deactivation, company cash inflow/outflow and recorded inter-account transfer reuse `BankCashProposalCard` and the deterministic Adaptive Proposal Review Rule. Small decisions expose complete account identity, supplied facts and readable before/after values inline in the owning `ProposalCardShell`. More than three metadata comparisons retain one wide, content-sized `FormSheet` with preserved dismissal: desktop places `ReviewCollection` / `ReviewItem` changes in the main pane and concise changed-field/stored-balance facts plus protected actions in the right aside; mobile reads those same summary facts before changed fields and keeps actions in the bottom footer. Bank, account-number or holder changes, nonzero opening balance, cash movement and transfer add one short shared `ConfirmationDialog` repeating account identity and the reviewed effect. Cash confirmations lead with nominal, date and reference, followed by source/destination facts, before account-balance comparisons. Plain metadata/theme/status changes and zero-balance account creation retain an explicit direct save. Reuse divided, wrapping `FactRow`, `ProposalDiffRow` with `strikeBefore={false}` and shared `MoneyValue` with `variant="fullDynamic"` for complete, unwrapped rupiah values. Shared adaptive `SheetFooterActions` keeps quiet correction before primary commit inline, primary-first stacked actions in desktop review asides and adaptive mobile pairs; confirmations reuse the adaptive shared action layout and standard primary tone. Corrections through chat request a fresh immutable preview. Account-read permission and source denial govern identity, facts and comparisons; blocked feedback stays after identity and before values, with recovery attached to its message. Current action rights, ready server proof, streaming, pending, stale/expired and error guards protect saving; a pending save prevents repeat submission and dismissal, and only explicit human approval sends the stored proposal identity. Model previews remain read-only. Saved receipts name the completed account/cash action and lead to “Buka rekening dan kas”. Deactivation retains stored balance/history; cash entry records company cash in Atria, and transfer records both account effects while total cash stays unchanged. Recording never sends a transfer to the bank. The family inherits Atria’s cool canvas, Manrope, white grouped owners, quiet capsules and shared focus, sizing, dismissal and motion without new tokens or another overlay owner.

rules.name: The AI Bank Reconciliation Review Rule
rules.body: AI bank-statement import, matching and exception marking/clearing reuse `ReconciliationWorkflowCard`, with actual account identity and the reviewed effect in the owning `ProposalCardShell`. Multirow imports and matches retain one wide, content-sized `FormSheet` with preserved dismissal: desktop keeps contextual `ReviewCollection` and `ReviewItem` rows in the main pane and concise grouped summary facts with protected actions in the right aside; mobile reads the same summary before rows and keeps actions in the bottom footer. A single mutation or exception decision stays inline. Paginate five rows at every width and retain page, selection, candidate choice, editor and overlay ownership through resize and reopening. Each mutation shows its description, date, translated direction, complete nominal and source, duplicate status or chosen Atria record. Reuse the contextual `ChoiceRow` review inclusion beside shared quiet Edit / Ringkas controls, without a leading checkbox column. Keep one shared inline editor open at a time; import corrections use embedded `FormSection` and the existing date, direction, text and money controls, with explicit “Terapkan koreksi” separate from business confirmation. Matching uses the shared selector for readable candidate dates, references and exception context; ambiguous candidates require an explicit choice. Selection and candidate choices update immediately and persist without replacing the review with a loading skeleton; business confirmation waits for acknowledgement and completed corrections. Summaries separate selected incoming and outgoing totals and show duplicate count for import or remaining unselected count for matching. Reuse divided, wrapping `FactRow` and `MoneyValue` with `variant="fullDynamic"` for complete, unwrapped rupiah values. Every save requires one short shared `ConfirmationDialog` with flat reviewed facts inside its existing owner, rather than another nested summary surface. Exception cards and confirmations show the nominal once, readable before/after status and the supplied human reason. Shared adaptive `SheetFooterActions` keeps quiet correction before commit inline, primary-first stacked desktop aside actions and adaptive mobile pairs. Account/source denial hides unavailable facts; recovery stays with `ProposalReviewFeedback` after account identity and before reviewed values. Current permissions, owned-source proof, draft revision, streaming, pending, stale/expired and conflict barriers guard explicit approval and prevent repeated saves or pending dismissal. Saved receipts identify the selected import/match outcome or changed exception status and lead to “Buka rekonsiliasi”. Import stores bank mutations for later matching; matching pairs existing records; exception decisions update reviewed status without creating cash, moving balances or changing stock. This family inherits Atria’s cool canvas, Manrope, white grouped owners and shared quiet controls, focus, dismissal, sizing and motion without new tokens or another overlay owner.

rules.name: The Shared Table Header Rule
rules.body: Page desktop tables retain HeroUI primary-table grammar: `surface-container-low` cohesive outer frame, header and footer, `on-surface-variant` column labels, white body rows and native table geometry. Keep sorting, hover/selection, disabled treatment, keyboard focus, cell density and supplied domain order intact. AI chat Markdown tables retain the same desktop page-table header tone and their existing mobile header treatment. This table grammar applies to deliberate tabular workflows; modal reviews follow the shared grouped-review contract and have no blanket HeroUI table requirement. Mobile review collections keep white divided grouped rows. Express table and surface separation through existing semantic tokens.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Terracotta is the only hue in the system. Warning and critical are the same family at different intensity, not different colors. Healthy, completed, pending, and inactive states stay neutral ink/gray with icon and copy carrying the meaning — never assign a fourth or fifth "status color."

rules.name: The No-Warm-Neutral Rule
rules.body: Neutral surfaces never take on cream, beige, brown, red, or yellow undertones. A neutral is always drawn from the cool ink/gray/canvas family above, never approximated with a warm gray utility because it "looks close."

rules.name: The Tabular Money Rule
rules.body: Every monetary value uses tabular numerals (`font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`) so digits never shift width as they change. Primary values stay on one line at 320–430px; when a full amount is too long, show a compact primary value with an exact secondary value alongside, never a wrapped primary.

rules.name: The One Role Rule
rules.body: Pick the semantic type role whose purpose matches, not the one whose pixel size happens to look close. An arbitrary size remains valid only for something with no role in this table.

rules.name: The Editable Text Rule
rules.body: On viewports below 1024px or devices with a coarse pointer, editable text inputs and textareas have a 16px minimum (`--text-input-min`). The shared stylesheet raises small type roles on the control itself, including grouped forms, money/quantity controls, search, chat, and HEX entry. Larger text keeps its size; labels, helper copy, read-only facts, and fine-pointer desktop controls keep their compact roles. Keep manual pinch zoom available.

rules.name: The Nested-Stays-Flat Rule
rules.body: A surface that sits inside another owner, or that is deliberately recessed, carries no lift: inset metric cells, icon tiles, metric pills, grouped form rows, and segmented-tab tracks. Elevation marks what owns hierarchy, so applying it to a nested element destroys the signal.

rules.name: The Lift-Is-Not-Loud Rule
rules.body: The resting lift must stay imperceptible element-by-element. If a shadow is legible on its own, it belongs to floating chrome (`raised`/`floating`/`sheet`/`overlay`), not to a resting surface — and if a static card reaches for `shadow-floating`, the role is wrong, not the value.

rules.name: The Selection-Stays-Flat Rule
rules.body: Selection and searchable-selection dialogs use one compact inset white option group with shared dividers. A selected row keeps the same white surface and is identified by a terracotta label plus check, never by another nested owner card or full-row tint.

rules.name: The Desktop Selection Interaction Rule
rules.body: Shared desktop plain, search and filter selectors can open an empty collection to show truthful empty guidance, while existing search, custom-value entry and explicit create actions remain available. Intentional options with an empty value, such as Tidak ditautkan, remain valid choices rather than being treated as no options. Dependent features may explicitly disable a selector for an unavailable prerequisite, with visible project/budget or recovery guidance; existing pending and permission guards remain authoritative. Public Button and IconButton forward the caller ref to the actual button DOM node in both mobile and desktop presentations, including tooltip-wrapped icon controls, so the shared HeroUI anchored owner controls positioning, outside dismissal and focus restoration. Selection updates the existing draft callback; business mutation keeps its explicit action. Create/menu handoffs use the shared exit queue, category/project confirmations retain their existing workflow owner, and nested selects/menus inherit the active sheet layer and shared focus/dismissal coordination. Escape closes the top surface while preserving the parent draft; feature code adds no portal or focus owner.

rules.name: The Field-Association Rule
rules.body: FormField owns one stable label/control/message relationship. Shared controls inherit its generated ID, required state, invalid state, and helper or error description unless an explicit caller value is supplied. Read-only facts and choice groups use their own row or fieldset semantics instead of an orphaned label.

rules.name: The Declared-Dismissal Rule
rules.body: Every editable form sheet declares whether close discards ephemeral input, confirms local dirty state, preserves parent or draft state, or delegates to an existing managed Save Draft / Discard / Continue flow. Backdrop, Escape, pull or header close, and programmatic close follow the same policy path.

rules.name: The One-Overlay-Owner Rule
rules.body: Calendar, media preview, selection, search, confirmation, and morph-detail wrappers use the internal DialogFrame for focus, visual viewport, body lock, Escape, reduced motion, and layering. Raw DialogFrame never crosses into feature code. Shared sheet chrome owns the opt-in desktop aside: `desktopAsideSummary` scrolls in a padded region above protected footer actions. The invisible aside reserves 256px for 224px content with 16px shadow gutters, preserving header/body alignment. Intrinsic summary and action heights determine natural sizing and viewport caps; feature code supplies content without a nested scroll owner, and bottom-footer behavior remains the default. At desktop widths, the viewport host centers the relative sheet using its actual animated height throughout expansion, collapse and reversal. Never derive its top offset from the target height. At disclosure animation start, shared infrastructure measures the final intrinsic layout height and restores temporary measurement styles before paint. Desktop sheet height and disclosure reveal both use `transitionEaseSmooth` so they settle together, without chasing intermediate resize frames. Non-disclosure size changes and sheet entrance/exit retain `transitionSpringSmooth`; mobile sheets keep their existing motion path and absolute bottom anchoring. The private shared controller owns this coordination; feature consumers do not duplicate it.

rules.name: The Stable Workspace Rule
rules.body: Providers, route children, draft/selection state and portal owners stay mounted across resize. Layout changes without navigation or a new session. A focused control or open overlay retains its control presentation until the interaction ends, so resize does not replace its DOM, focus owner or dismissal policy.

rules.name: Read-only pull dismissal
rules.body: DetailSheet may opt into dismissOnPull for short introductions such as Panduan Peran. On mobile a downward pull from natural height uses the same onClose path as X, backdrop and Escape; expanded sheets first collapse. Non-resizable handles support keyboard close. Default sheets retain resize-only gestures.

rules.name: The Disclosure Motion Rule
rules.body: Accordion and disclosure headers, including every `FormDisclosure` variant, keep native button semantics and never scale on press or tap. Expansion retains the chevron rotation and content height/opacity reveal through the shared motion presets. Disclosure spacing belongs to padding inside the animated clipped content and collapses with it. Reduced motion makes the reveal and chevron change immediate. Ordinary action `Button` and `IconButton` controls, including navigation and edit actions, retain their existing press-scale behavior.

rules.name: The AI Desktop Form Panel Rule
rules.body: Material Master review, single/batch correction and reference creation, plus assistant preferences, use the shared wide, content-sized `FormSheet` layout on desktop. `OperationalFormSheet` and `WorkflowFormSheet` forward the existing desktop size, footer placement and aside summary slots without changing their default behavior. The left column owns fields or reviewed rows; the right aside owns concise draft readiness/reference counts or selected preference facts and protected actions. Shared `SheetFooterActions` stacks full-width action buttons in desktop asides while retaining its two-button mobile footer and accessible disabled-reason guards. Material counts and blockers move to the aside only on desktop; mobile retains its established single-column summary/blocker sequence and bottom actions. Reuse `GroupedSurface`, divided `FactRow` values and the existing aside shadow gutters, sizing, focus, dismissal and motion coordinator. Keep draft/selection/editor state above responsive changes, five-row Material pagination, metadata correction separate from business Save, and reference creation separate from material creation. Preferences retain permission-filtered focus options, dirty dismissal, Save and Reset. Compact rename and destructive confirmations remain focused decision dialogs; the composer wizard remains in the composer.

rules.name: The AI Review Feedback Rule
rules.body: Blocking and validation feedback in adaptive chat-card reviews and retained review sheets belongs after entity/project identity and before reviewed values or rows. Compose the feature-level `ProposalReviewFeedback` from shared `GroupedSurface`, `InlineStateRow` and `Button`; preserve the exact server message, a concise heading and a semantic status icon. Use its `embedded` presentation inside `ProposalCardShell` so the existing card remains the sole surface and shadow owner; retained sheets keep the grouped feedback surface. Keep any recovery control with its message: trailing in the wide desktop content row, below the description on mobile through the optional shared `InlineStateRow actionPlacement` contract. The default trailing placement remains unchanged for other consumers. Use the shared quiet compact button so recovery stays subordinate to the business decision. The chat-card action area, retained-sheet desktop aside and mobile protected footer contain commit/correction controls and ordinary state guidance, without loose error text or a detached retry after them. Field-specific validation remains next to its fields, permissions and confirmation barriers remain authoritative, and the existing Material Master selection/analysis feedback flow retains its domain context. Status changes reuse the existing card or sheet sizing and motion owner; no new surface, motion, focus or touch-target primitive is introduced.

rules.name: The Budget Summary Inspection Rule
rules.body: Budget summary inspections use the existing proposal family: project identity and a compact matching/differing verdict precede up to three actual labeled before/after differences in `ProposalCardShell`; a contextual detail action opens the full inspection. Clean results have no synchronization action, while critical or over-budget conditions remain visible even when summaries match. Optional read-only `FormSheet` detail uses one grouped `ReviewCollection`/`ReviewItem`, at most five category rows per page and one open detail; desktop keeps summary/actions in the shared aside, while mobile stacks summary above rows and uses bottom actions. Preserve page, disclosure and overlay state through resize and reopening. Reuse `ProposalInlineReview`/`ProposalDiffRow`, divided `FactRow` and `MoneyValue` with `variant="fullDynamic"` for complete, unwrapped amounts. Explicit synchronization opens shared `ConfirmationDialog` naming project, changed categories and actual changed fields; a pending, paid or status-only correction must not imply changed consumption. Keep stale/expired, access and uncertain-outcome feedback beside its recovery action. The saved verdict distinguishes a recorded sync from a freshly verified persisted result; synchronization updates derived usage only, without implying changes to cash, stock, contract, cap or allocations. No new visual tokens or overlay owner are introduced.

rules.name: The AI Activity Outcome Rule
rules.body: AI activity uses shared `FormDisclosure` with `variant="activity"`: one compact contextual summary, no extra surface, and details opened by the reader. The summary reflects the current task outcome, with running work, unresolved failures and stopped work taking priority over waiting or completion. A recovered read remains in the flat semantic history as a neutral refresh icon with visible “Pulih”; it is not a current failure. Recovery requires a later genuine result from the same tool with the same canonical inputs within the same assistant message, preserving target, filters and page. The bounded historical exception is a one-character project-search validation failure followed by a scoped project list whose actual results supply the subsequent project-selector options. A different tool or target, access denial, mutation, interruption, missing result or structured output error cannot establish recovery. Expanded unresolved steps show fixed, safe category guidance without raw inputs, values or error strings. Waiting follows the active input request and its current wizard values: an unselected required project shows “Pilih proyek untuk melanjutkan”; a valid project selection shows “Menunggu isian Anda”. Submitted, cancelled or dismissed requests stop waiting while recovered history remains. Details keep small shared `ActivityMark` / `AppIcon` state icons, accessible completion text and visible running, failed, recovered and stopped labels without elevation or repeated completion badges. Waiting uses a static clock; only running activity loops, using unified motion presets with reduced-motion and visibility support.

rules.name: The Manual Desktop Form Panel Rule
rules.body: Meaningful manual input and review sheets use the existing wide, content-sized FormSheet with desktopFooterPlacement="aside" and desktopAsideSummary. The main pane owns editable fields and reviewed rows; the right pane owns live draft context and protected existing actions. Reuse OperationalFormSheet, WorkflowFormSheet, GroupedSurface and SheetFooterActions. Narrow aside facts use FactRow layout="stacked" so labels and long values remain readable; its default inline contract stays unchanged. dos: Do keep exactly one accent hue (terracotta) system-wide; express urgency through its intensity (`#b84b2c` → `#97371f`), never through a new hue.

Do give every owning surface and standalone control its semantic resting lift (`shadow-surface`/`shadow-control`, or the dark-tier `shadow-primary`/`shadow-inverse`), and keep everything nested inside one flat.
Do keep every standalone interactive control a full capsule, and every container surface on the fixed 28/20/16px radius scale — never mix the two vocabularies.
Do keep primary monetary values on one line with tabular numerals at 320–430px, falling back to a compact value + exact secondary value when the full amount is too long.
Do combine status with copy and an icon/shape/position — never color alone.
Do keep motion purposeful and spring-based (`lib/utils/motion.ts` presets only) — selection, origin, continuity, feedback.
Do keep selection/search options in one compact inset white group and indicate selection with terracotta label plus the shared check glyph rather than a filled rectangle.
Do let FormField create and propagate the accessible label, control, helper, and error relationship by default.
Do declare discard, confirm, preserve, or managed dismissal behavior on every editable form sheet.
Do keep all modal focus, viewport, dismissal, reduced-motion, and layering behavior behind semantic shared wrappers.
Do put simple repeated events, transactions, and master-data rows on one grouped surface with dividers; reserve an individual card for a genuinely independent, decision-heavy entity.

Do keep every main route's `loading.tsx` a structural skeleton matching the final hierarchy (header/tabs, focal summary, expected rows, nav clearance) — never a centered spinner or generic loading card.

Do keep mobile/coarse-pointer effective touch targets at 48×48px even when the visible control is smaller; use compact shared 32–40px controls on fine-pointer desktop. Preserve keyboard focus order, screen-reader labels, safe-area clearance, and reduced-motion behavior throughout.
donts: Don't add a second or third accent color, a rainbow of category colors, or a locally-defined focus-ring color.

Don't hand-roll a shadow value or reach past the semantic role — no `shadow-[...]`, no raw `box-shadow`, and no `shadow-floating` on a static card. Never put a lift on a nested row, icon tile, metric cell, or recessed tab track, and never apply blur or glass to an ordinary surface.
Don't use glassmorphism, decorative gradients, or oversized touch chrome anywhere except a configured bank-account identity surface (the sole user-defined gradient exception).
Don't wrap a primary money value, or let a value's digits reflow without tabular numerals.

Don't add whole-page transitions, section entrances, or list-stagger animation — routes, tabs, and lists stay visually instant; only the active-pill spring and explicit local feedback (taps, sheets, disclosures) animate.
Don't warm a neutral surface with cream, beige, brown, red, or yellow undertones.

Don't ship a generic admin-dashboard or spreadsheet-like composition — a repeated formula of summary card, header pill, and identical rounded cards for every section is a tell that the content pattern wasn't chosen deliberately.

Don't use an inset metric grid for a single title/meta/value row, activity/history/transactions, or more than three equal-weight cells in one mobile row; don't give a metric cell its own shadow, elevation, or oversized radius that competes with its owning surface.

Don't nest a capsule inside another owning surface for ordinary grouped rows, or place a colored vertical severity rail or short attention marker beside an ordinary list icon — a continuous connector is timeline-only.
Don't add another owner card inside the shared option group or tint the full selected row.
Don't leave a hidden action or an ambiguous icon-only control without an accessible label, or build UI from placeholder/dummy data when real domain data exists.
